learn.hook: For more than 300 years, five different ruling families took turns on one throne in Delhi. Who were they?
points: The Delhi Sultanate began in 1206 CE, when Qutb-ud-din Aibak became Sultan in Delhi. It lasted until 1526 CE.
Five dynasties ruled one after another: the Mamluks (also called the Slave dynasty), the Khaljis, the Tughlaqs, the Sayyids and the Lodis.
Razia Sultan ruled from 1236 to 1240 CE. She was the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate.

Alauddin Khalji fixed the prices of goods in Delhi's markets and kept a large army that pushed back several Mongol attacks. Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) and introduced token coins of copper and brass.
In 1398 CE, Timur from Central Asia attacked and plundered Delhi, which weakened the Sultanate. The last Sultan, Ibrahim Lodi, was defeated by Babur in 1526 CE.

example.q: Think it through: Muhammad bin Tughlaq's token coins failed. Why might token money fail if it is easy to copy?
steps: A token coin is worth more than the metal it is made of; its value depends on the ruler's order.
Copper and brass were easy to get, so many people made fake coins at home.
The market was flooded with coins and people lost trust in them.
The Sultan had to withdraw the coins and exchange them for real gold and silver ones.
example.answer: Because the coins could be forged easily, too many fake coins spread, trust collapsed and the scheme had to be withdrawn.

learn.reallife: You can still visit the Qutub Minar in Delhi, begun by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by Iltutmish, and the ruins of Tughlaqabad fort.

games.title: Who did what?
pairs: Only woman ruler of the Sultanate

quiz.q: In which year did the Delhi Sultanate begin?
quiz.explain: Qutb-ud-din Aibak became Sultan in 1206 CE, starting the Delhi Sultanate.
steps: Qutb-ud-din Aibak became Sultan in Delhi in 1206 CE.
That marks the start of the Delhi Sultanate.
1526 is when it ended.
Answer: 1206
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the start of the Sultanate with later events

quiz.q: Which was the last dynasty of the Delhi Sultanate?
quiz.explain: The Lodis ruled last; Ibrahim Lodi lost to Babur in 1526.
steps: Five dynasties: Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi.
The Lodis came last; Ibrahim Lodi lost to Babur in 1526.
Answer: Lodi
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the order of the dynasties

quiz.q: Who was the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate?
quiz.explain: Razia, daughter of Iltutmish, ruled from 1236 to 1240 CE.
steps: Razia Sultan ruled from 1236 to 1240 CE.
She was the only woman to rule the Delhi Sultanate.
Answer: Razia Sultan
quiz.mistake: Confuses women rulers from different periods

quiz.q: Which Sultan moved his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad?
quiz.explain: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted the capital to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in the Deccan.
steps: Muhammad bin Tughlaq shifted his capital from Delhi to Daulatabad (Devagiri) in the Deccan.
Answer: Muhammad bin Tughlaq
quiz.mistake: Mixes up the policies of different Sultans

quiz.q: Alauddin Khalji is remembered for:
quiz.explain: He set fixed prices for goods like grain so that his large army could be paid and fed.
steps: Alauddin Khalji fixed prices of goods in Delhi's markets.
This helped him pay and feed his large army.
Answer: Controlling prices in Delhi's markets
quiz.mistake: Mixes up rulers of different periods

quiz.q: Which Central Asian ruler attacked and plundered Delhi in 1398 CE?
quiz.explain: Timur's attack in 1398 weakened the Delhi Sultanate.
steps: In 1398 CE Timur from Central Asia attacked and plundered Delhi.
This weakened the Sultanate.
Answer: Timur
quiz.mistake: Confuses different invaders from Central Asia

quiz.q: Who began building the Qutub Minar in Delhi?
quiz.explain: Aibak began it and his successor Iltutmish completed it.
steps: Qutb-ud-din Aibak began building the Qutub Minar.
His successor Iltutmish completed it.
Answer: Qutb-ud-din Aibak
quiz.mistake: Links the minar with later Mughal builders

quiz.q: How many years did the Delhi Sultanate last, from 1206 to 1526?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the years carelessly
steps: End year 1526 minus start year 1206
Answer: 320

teach.ask: Gappu is confused by so many Sultans. Explain the Delhi Sultanate to Gappu: when it began, when it ended and who ruled.
teach.praise: Five families on one throne for 320 years! Now I can tell them apart.
teach.nudge: When did it start and end? Can you name some of the ruling families?

revise.summary: The Delhi Sultanate (1206–1526 CE) was ruled by the Mamluks, Khaljis, Tughlaqs, Sayyids and Lodis. Key rulers include Razia Sultan, Alauddin Khalji (price control) and Muhammad bin Tughlaq (capital shift, token coins). Timur's raid (1398) weakened it.
focus: Dates and the five dynasties in order
Key rulers and what each did
Why the Sultanate weakened and ended
remember: 1206 CE: Qutb-ud-din Aibak; 1526 CE: Ibrahim Lodi defeated by Babur
Dynasties: Mamluk, Khalji, Tughlaq, Sayyid, Lodi
traps: Muhammad bin Tughlaq, not Alauddin Khalji, moved the capital to Daulatabad
The Lodis, not the Tughlaqs, were the last dynasty
Razia Sultan, not Nur Jahan, ruled the Sultanate

learn.hook: In 1526 a ruler from Central Asia won a battle at Panipat with the help of cannons and guns. His family would rule for over 300 years.
points: Babur, a ruler from Fergana in Central Asia, defeated Ibrahim Lodi at the First Battle of Panipat in 1526 and founded the Mughal empire. He used cannons and guns along with skilled cavalry.

His son Humayun lost his kingdom to Sher Shah Suri in 1540 and won it back in 1555. Sher Shah improved roads such as the one now called the Grand Trunk Road and issued a silver coin called the rupiya.
Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605. He organised officials through the mansabdari system, in which each officer held a rank, and followed a policy of sulh-i-kul, peace among all.
Later emperors were Jahangir, Shah Jahan, who built the Taj Mahal, and Aurangzeb, who ruled from 1658 to 1707. Under Aurangzeb the empire reached its largest size.
After Aurangzeb died in 1707, the empire grew weak and many regional powers, such as the Marathas, rose.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the mansabdari system help Akbar control a huge empire?
steps: Every mansabdar (officer) was given a rank (mansab).
The rank decided his pay and the number of soldiers and horses he had to keep.
Mansabdars could be transferred and promoted or demoted by the emperor.
So all officers depended on the emperor, and he always had an army ready.
example.answer: It ranked every officer, tied their pay to soldiers they maintained and kept them loyal to the emperor, giving him a ready army and an organised government.

learn.reallife: The word 'rupee' on our banknotes comes from the rupiya, the silver coin issued by Sher Shah Suri.

Answer: Sher Shah Suri

Akbar respected people of different faiths.

quiz.q: Under which emperor did the Mughal empire reach its largest size?
quiz.explain: Aurangzeb extended Mughal rule far into the Deccan.
steps: Aurangzeb (1658–1707) extended Mughal rule deep into the Deccan.
The empire reached its largest size under him.
Answer: Aurangzeb
quiz.mistake: Assumes Akbar ruled the largest area

quiz.q: Which Mughal emperor built the Taj Mahal?
quiz.explain: Shah Jahan built it in Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
steps: Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal in Agra in memory of his wife Mumtaz Mahal.
Answer: Shah Jahan
quiz.mistake: Mixes up Mughal builders

quiz.q: In a mansab, the rank of an officer decided:
options: His pay and the number of soldiers and horses he kept
quiz.explain: Rank fixed salary and military duties.
steps: Each mansabdar held a rank (mansab).
The rank decided his pay and the soldiers and horses he had to keep.
Answer: His pay and the number of soldiers and horses he kept
quiz.mistake: Does not understand how the mansabdari system worked

quiz.q: Akbar ruled from 1556 to 1605. For about how many years did he rule?
quiz.mistake: Subtracts carelessly
steps: = 49 years
Answer: 49

teach.ask: Gappu wants a short story of the Mughals. Explain who started the empire, one great ruler and when it began to decline.
teach.praise: From Babur to Aurangzeb, I can now draw the Mughal family tree!
teach.nudge: Who started it and when? What happened after 1707?

revise.summary: Babur founded the Mughal empire after the First Battle of Panipat (1526). Humayun lost to Sher Shah Suri and regained his throne. Akbar ruled through the mansabdari system and sulh-i-kul; Shah Jahan built the Taj Mahal; the empire was largest under Aurangzeb.
focus: Order of major Mughal rulers and their achievements
remember: Sher Shah: Grand Trunk Road, silver rupiya
traps: Babur, not Akbar, founded the Mughal empire
Shah Jahan, not Akbar, built the Taj Mahal
Mansab rank decided pay and soldiers, not religion or birthplace

learn.hook: While Delhi saw Sultans and Mughals, powerful kingdoms ruled the Deccan, Rajasthan, Gondwana and Assam, and many of them fought hard to stay free.
points: The Vijayanagara empire was founded in 1336 by the brothers Harihara and Bukka. Its capital, Vijayanagara (Hampi), lay on the Tungabhadra river and was a rich trading city.
Krishnadevaraya was Vijayanagara's most famous ruler. In 1565, at the Battle of Talikota, an alliance of Deccan Sultanates defeated Vijayanagara and the capital was ruined.
Rajput rulers of Mewar resisted the Mughals. Rana Sanga fought Babur at Khanwa in 1527, and Maharana Pratap fought Akbar's army at Haldighati in 1576.
Rani Durgavati of Garha-Katanga (in Gondwana, central India) fought Mughal forces bravely in 1564.
The Ahoms of Assam resisted the Mughals. In 1671, their commander Lachit Borphukan won the Battle of Saraighat on the Brahmaputra river.

example.q: Think it through: Why did the Brahmaputra help the Ahoms at Saraighat?
steps: The battle was fought on the river near Guwahati.
The Ahoms knew the river, its currents and its narrow points well.
They used boats skilfully and built defences along the banks.
So the Mughal fleet could not use its larger numbers well.
example.answer: The Ahoms used their knowledge of the river and good boat warfare, so the geography worked in their favour.

learn.reallife: You can walk among the ruins of Hampi in Karnataka, a UNESCO World Heritage Site. The National Defence Academy awards a Lachit Borphukan gold medal to its best cadet.

Answer: Lachit Borphukan

quiz.explain: It was fought in 1671 near Guwahati.
steps: The Battle of Saraighat was fought in 1671 near Guwahati.
Answer: 1671

quiz.q: Rani Durgavati ruled the kingdom of:
quiz.explain: She was the queen of Garha-Katanga in central India.
steps: Rani Durgavati was queen of Garha-Katanga in Gondwana, central India.
Answer: Garha-Katanga in Gondwana
quiz.mistake: Confuses different women rulers and regions

quiz.q: Rana Sanga of Mewar fought Babur at Khanwa in 1527. How many years was this after the First Battle of Panipat (1526)?
steps: Khanwa was in 1527; Panipat was in 1526.
So it was 1 year later.
Answer: 1
quiz.mistake: Does not compare the two dates

teach.ask: Gappu thinks only Delhi mattered in this period. Explain to Gappu about other kingdoms that ruled and resisted.
teach.praise: So many brave kingdoms all over India! The map kept changing.
teach.nudge: What about the south and the north-east? Who resisted the Mughals?

revise.summary: Vijayanagara (1336, Harihara and Bukka, capital Hampi on the Tungabhadra) peaked under Krishnadevaraya and fell after Talikota (1565). Rana Sanga, Maharana Pratap, Rani Durgavati and the Ahoms under Lachit Borphukan resisted the Mughals.
focus: Battles of resistance and their dates
remember: Khanwa 1527 (Rana Sanga vs Babur); Haldighati 1576 (Maharana Pratap)
Saraighat 1671: Lachit Borphukan on the Brahmaputra
traps: Haldighati was Maharana Pratap's battle; Khanwa was Rana Sanga's
Hampi is on the Tungabhadra, not the Ganga
